question: 16 men can complete a work in 15 days. How many men are required to complete the same work in 10 days?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The work is inversely proportional to the number of men.

Men required = (Initial men × Initial days) ÷ New days

⇒ Men required = (16 × 15) ÷ 10 = 24 men

**∴ Answer = 24 men**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

16 men can complete the work in 15 days. Number of men required to complete the same work in 10 days = ?

**Formula used:**

Men required = (Initial men × Initial days) ÷ New days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Men required = (16 × 15) ÷ 10

⇒ Men required = 240 ÷ 10

⇒ Men required = 24 men

**∴ The correct answer is 24 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality Rule

When two quantities are inversely proportional, the product of the two remains constant. Example: Men × Days = Constant.

Work and Time Relationship

If the amount of work remains constant, increasing the number of workers reduces the required time proportionally.

LCM Method for Work

LCM is often used in work problems to find the total work, especially when multiple workers are involved with different efficiencies.
